clusters.state_of_play: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president on Monday, effective immediately, less than two weeks after he resigned on Nov. 12 amid reports of multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a woman suspected of spying for China, and reportedly with employees. Huang got a hero's welcome at HQ. NYT reports US intelligence tracked her contacts with China's Ministry of State Security. The US is probing Alice Huang and Singapore-based Megaspeed, the firm at the heart of the chip case. Commerce is set to add Megaspeed to the trade blacklist, requiring a license for US chip sales to it. Trump and Vance reportedly intervened; Axios sources say allies argued Huang was too big to fail and a victim of deep state maneuvering. Trump told CNBC he spoke to the board and to Xi about Huang, that Huang did nothing wrong, and that the board sought national security assurances. He cited the attorney general and urged Nvidia to continue its export-control investigation. The board cited input from senior levels of government, and a probe into Huang's conduct is reportedly ongoing. Interim CEO Kress and senior management were not consulted. Stock jumped about 31.5% Monday, adding about $1 trillion in value, then fell 6-7% on Tuesday as the rally cooled. Huang faces a Washington grilling the same day as Nvidia's GTC product launches. Lawmakers in both parties criticize the move. Jeffries wants export controls added to the defense policy bill.
